text:
iMCP is a macOS app for connecting your digital life with AI.
It works with [Claude Desktop][claude-app],
the [ChatGPT desktop app][chatgpt-app],
local models served by [llama.cpp][llama-cpp],
and a [growing list of clients][mcp-clients] that support the
[Model Context Protocol (MCP)][mcp].

 Capabilities

 
 
 
 
 
 Calendar 
 View and manage calendar events, including creating new events with customizable settings like recurrence, alarms, and availability status. 
 
 
 
 
 
 Contacts 
 Access contact information about yourself and search your contacts by name, phone number, or email address. 
 
 
 
 
 
 Home 
 Find homes, rooms, accessories, scenes, and automations, read and control accessories, and organize rooms and zones. Needs a helper app that you build with your own Apple Developer account . 
 
 
 
 
 
 Location 
 Access current location data and convert between addresses and geographic coordinates. 
 
 
 
 
 
 Mail 
 List mailboxes, search messages by sender, subject, mailbox, date, or read status, read messages stored on your Mac, and open new drafts in your default email app. Reading mail needs access to your Mail folder . 
 
 
 
 
 
 Maps 
 Provides location services including place search, directions, points of interest lookup, travel time estimation, and static map image generation. 
 
 
 
 
 
 Messages 
 Access message history with specific participants within customizable date ranges. 
 
 
 
 
 
 Music 
 See what's playing in the Music app, control playback, list your playlists and their tracks, and search the Apple Music catalog. Playback and playlist tools need Automation permission for Music; catalog search needs Apple Music access. 
 
 
 
 
 
 Notes 
 Search notes by text, folder, or date, and read them as Markdown with their checklists, tables, and links. 
 
 
 
 
 
 Phone 
 View call history synced from your iPhone, filter calls by participant, date, or call type, and start calls with system confirmation. 
 
 
 
 
 
 Reminders 
 View, create, edit, and delete reminders with customizable due dates, recurrence, priorities, and alerts across different reminder lists, and manage the lists themselves. 
 
 
 
 
 
 Shortcuts 
 List and run shortcuts on your Mac, with optional text input. 
 
 
 
 
 
 Voice Memos 
 Fetch recordings from Voice Memos, with transcripts and audio, filtering by title, folder, or date, or reading Recently Deleted. Needs access to your Voice Memos folder . 
 
 
 
 
 
 Voicemail 
 Fetch voicemails synced from your iPhone, with transcripts and audio, filtering by sender, date, message type, or mailbox (inbox, blocked, or deleted). 
 
 
 
 
 
 Weather 
 Access current weather conditions including temperature, wind speed, and weather conditions for any location.

install.title: Getting Started
install.html:
To use iMCP, you need two apps: iMCP, which gives access to the services you turn on, and an AI app that can connect to MCP servers. Install iMCP and turn on services first. Then follow the instructions for your AI app:

  • Claude Desktop
  • ChatGPT desktop app
  • Claude Code, llama.cpp, and other clients
Download and open the app

First, download the iMCP app (requires macOS 15.3 or later).

Or, if you have Homebrew installed, you can run the following command:

brew install --cask mattt/tap/iMCP

When you open the app, you'll see a icon in your menu bar.

Click this icon to open the iMCP menu. The blue "Enable MCP Server" switch at the top indicates that the MCP server is running and ready to connect with AI apps. iMCP must be open for AI apps to use it.

Below the switch, the menu lists the available services. Maps is on when you first open iMCP; the other services are off and appear in gray. iMCP also includes a tool that plays a system sound. That tool is always available, even with every service off, so you can test a connection without granting any permissions.


Turn on services

To turn on a service, click its icon. macOS asks you for permission. For example, when you turn on Calendar, a dialog asks "'iMCP' Would Like Full Access to Your Calendar". Click "Allow Full Access" to continue.

[!IMPORTANT] iMCP does not collect or store any of your data. AI apps like Claude and ChatGPT do send your data off device as part of tool calls. Turn on only the services you want your AI app to use. To keep your data on your Mac, use a local model with llama.cpp.


When a service is on, its icon changes from gray to the service's color: red for Calendar, green for Messages, blue for Location, and so on.

Repeat these steps for each service that you want to use. macOS asks for each permission separately, so iMCP can access only the data that you allow. To turn off a service, click its icon again. To turn off individual tools in a service, click > "Settings", and then click the service in the sidebar.


Approve connections

The first time an AI app connects, iMCP shows a "Client Connection Request" dialog with the name the app reports and the services that the app can use. Click "Allow" to connect. "Allow" turns on a second after the dialog opens, and pressing Return doesn't click it, so that a click or a key press meant for another window doesn't approve a client as the dialog opens. If you don't answer within two minutes, iMCP denies the connection. After you deny a client that presents a credential, iMCP denies connections with that credential without asking for 30 seconds. iMCP shows up to three dialogs at once, and refuses connections while "Enable MCP Server" is off.

Any app can report any name, so iMCP doesn't trust a client by its name. Instead, iMCP trusts a client that presents a credential iMCP created for it. imcp-server reads the credential from the IMCP_CLIENT_CREDENTIAL environment variable in the client's MCP settings, and sends it to iMCP after it checks that iMCP is genuine. iMCP stores only a hash of each credential, in your Keychain.

To skip the dialog next time, select "Always trust this client". If the client already presents a credential, for example because iMCP set up Claude Desktop, iMCP trusts that credential. Otherwise, iMCP creates a credential and shows it once. Click "Copy Value" and add IMCP_CLIENT_CREDENTIAL with that value to the environment of the iMCP server in the client's MCP settings. iMCP then shows a notification each time the client connects. You can remove trusted clients in > "Settings" > "Clients", which revokes their credentials and closes their connections.

[!NOTE] Earlier versions of iMCP trusted clients by name. Those clients need your approval again; select "Always trust this client" to give each one a credential.


Add a credential to a client's MCP settings

In a JSON configuration file, add the credential to the server's env:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "iMCP": {
      "command": "/Applications/iMCP.app/Contents/MacOS/imcp-server",
      "env": {
        "IMCP_CLIENT_CREDENTIAL": "{paste the copied value}"
      }
    }
  }
}

With Claude Code, add the server again with the -e option:

claude mcp remove --scope user iMCP
claude mcp add --scope user -e IMCP_CLIENT_CREDENTIAL={paste the copied value} \
  iMCP -- /Applications/iMCP.app/Contents/MacOS/imcp-server

Anyone who can read the client's settings can use the credential, so keep those files private to your user account. If you think that a credential was exposed, remove the client in "Settings" > "Clients" and trust it again.

Mail access and search

Mail store access uses Envelope, which reads the local index and message files and selects readable content with its internal MIME reader. iMCP manages folder access, tool arguments, JSON output, and composition.

Mail reading requires access to ~/Library/Mail. If folder access is unavailable, mail_compose can still open a compose window in the default email app. It does not save or send a message.

Mail reads use a read-only SQLite connection and require WAL journal mode. iMCP does not change the index's journal mode or run checkpoints. It permits one Mail database connection at a time; concurrent reads wait their turn, and a read returns an error if SQLite reports a lock conflict. Each SQL statement has a 100 ms execution budget, all statements of one read share a 1 s budget, and statements check task cancellation. The deadline is cooperative; it cannot interrupt a filesystem operation while SQLite is waiting for that operation to finish. Slow searches can fail instead of returning results. Service status checks do not open SQLite connections, and message reads close the database before scanning mailbox files. These limits reduce interference, but active reads can still delay WAL checkpoints.

Use the @id string from mail_mailboxes_list as the mailbox filter in mail_messages_search, for example {"mailbox": "V10:12"}. The identifier includes the Mail store, so an identifier from before a Mail store upgrade returns an error. The url field describes storage and is not a search identifier. Each mailbox includes an account identifier when available. The account's email field comes from Mail's local account map; it is null when that map is missing or does not contain an email address.

Search results include localIndex.indexedMessageCount for the selected mailbox, or all mailboxes when no mailbox is selected, before filters and pagination. This count includes label membership without counting a message twice. Sync status is reported as unknown. A count of zero can mean an empty mailbox or missing local indexing; it cannot show whether Mail has ever indexed the account. Open Mail to check account sync.

Search results are newest first. When more messages match, the result includes a nextCursor value; pass it as cursor with the same filters to get the next page. A cursor names the last message of a page, so mail that arrives between requests does not shift later pages.

Search matches sender and subject metadata only. mail_messages_read can read the local content of a returned message. It lists attachments without their content. When Mail stores a message's attachments or inline images in separate files, the message file keeps the text, and each of those attachments has isStoredSeparately set to true. Body search is not available, and these tools do not download messages.

Connect to Claude Desktop

If you don't have Claude Desktop installed, you can download it here.

usage.title: Using the MCP Inspector
usage.html:
To debug interactions between iMCP and clients, you can use the inspector tool (requires Node.js):

  1. Click > "Copy server command to clipboard"

  2. Open a terminal and run the following commands:

    # Download and run inspector package on imcp-server
npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector [paste-copied-command]

# Open inspector web app running locally
open http://127.0.0.1:6274

Inspector lets you see all requests and responses between the client and the iMCP server, which is helpful for understanding how the protocol works.
